headline: Approved prior meeting minutes and FY27 budget update for submission to City Council and Mayor, both 4-0.
summary: The committee approved minutes from three prior meetings and voted to submit the FY27 CPA budget update, which reflects a 15.5% state match estimate, to City Council and the Mayor. Members heard from Rev. Dr. Debora Jackson about Emmanuel Baptist Church's building conditions assessment and funding needs, discussed the annual CPA survey distribution, and reviewed the FY27 pre-application form without finalizing changes.
decisions: Approved the meeting minutes from December 17, 2025, January 21, 2026, and February 18, 2026, 4-0.
Approved submitting the FY27 CPA budget update to City Council and the Mayor, 4-0.
plain_text:
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 1 
  
  
  
   
  
  
Community Preservation Committee  
 
 
Malden City Hall Room #105 
Broadcast live and recorded on Teams 
March 18, 2026 | 6:00 p.m. 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Committee Members in Attendance: Rachael Running, Chair, Inna Babitskaya, Jamie Kendall, Brendan 
Brett  
Committee Members Absent: Ronnie Raj Verma, Sam Watters, Vice Chair, Monique Ching, 
CPC Manager: Daniel Koff  
 
1. Meeting Called to Order 
Running called the meeting to order at 6:06 p.m and conducted attendance.  
 
2. Approval of CPC Monthly Meeting minutes from December 17, 2025, January 21, 2026, February 18, 
2026 
Babitskaya made a motion to approve the meeting minutes from December 17, 2025, January 21, 2026, 
February 18, 2026, seconded by Brett. Approved 4-0.  
 
3. FY27 CPA Budget Update 
Running presented a budget update showing an estimated state match reflecting DOR’s estimate of 
15.5%.
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 2 
Kendall moved to submit the budget update to City Council and the Mayor. Brett seconded. Approved 4-
0.   
 
4. 0035_Emmanuel Baptist Church 
Koff provided an overview of the conditions assessment by GRLA that was conducted by Emmanuel 
Baptist Church as a basis for their updated application.  
Running invited Rev. Dr. Debora Jackson to speak on behalf of the Church and to answer CPC’s 
questions.  
Brett inquired as to whether the windows that were purchased as part of the botched renovation are 
still useable. Jackson was unaware. 
Kendall inquired as to whether CPA could reimburse the Church for their expenses on the $3,640 that 
was spent on the conditions assessment. Koff offered to look into it.  
Brett inquired whether additional costs were covered for potential ADA compliance. Jackson explained 
that those costs are included in the estimates.  
Jackson explained that they are looking at additional funders to pay for additional improvements.  
Kendall inquired whether the Church has capacity to update the fire alarm system and verbalized the 
risk of replacing the roof on a building that doesn’t have a fire suppression system. Jackson explained 
that they are making the system a priority.  
Running thanked Reverand Jackson for attending. 
 
5. Annual CPA Survey 
Koff explained that the survey went out in residents’ water bill and that 30 were printed for CPC 
members to distribute.  
Koff offered to share it on Facebook and to email the flyer to Sam to post on Reddit. 
Running inquired as to whether CPC should start an Instagram account to share the flyer and updates on 
parks.  
 
6. CPA Plan Update – Review of FY27 Pre-Application 
Running explained that the proposed FY27 application is a replica of the FY26 application and asked 
members if there is anything they would like to change.  
Kendall inquired about the guideline for having cost estimates to support the budget and whether 
Section 1, #9 still satisfies CPC’s intentions. Members decided to keep it as-is.
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 3 
Brett highlighted that the evaluation criteria about the desire to use CPA funds to leverage other sources 
is not well emphasized in the application instructions. He suggested putting the evaluation scorecard in 
the application instructions document.  
 
7. Other Business  
Brett inquired as to whether an organization with which he’s affiliated could apply for CPA Funds. 
Running explained that the organization would be encouraged to apply, although further due diligence 
would be needed to see if he could participate in the deliberation and vote on that project.  
 
5. Adjournment of CPC Monthly Meeting 
Brett made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Kendall seconded. Unanimously approved.
